policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the clause 'they went forward into the land' — a verb of motion with 'into', matching the ketiv ויבו 'they came (into it)'; the qere וַיַּכּוּ 'they smote (in it)' would have yielded a striking verb, which the ASV instead reserves for the following 'smiting the Moabites'. The hebrew_gloss note 'Hebrew into it' does not decide the reading but is consistent with 'into' translating בָהּ after a verb of entering.
